lead: jQuery is a small JavaScript library that wraps three common jobs — selecting elements, handling events and asking the server for data — into short calls that chain with dots. It exists because older browsers disagreed about the DOM and events, so the same code could fail on one browser and work on another. A student today meets it in legacy pages, in quick college projects and in plugins that still expect it. The core habit it teaches is: select a set, change the set, repeat. That habit carries into modern frameworks.
prereq: You need: 3.4 for DOM selection, 3.3 for events and 3.7 for AJAX.

sections.h3: The $ function and the jQuery object

blocks.text: jQuery is one .js file. Add it from a CDN before your own script, or use a local copy. The library defines a function named $, also written jQuery. With a string, $ selects.

$('#items li') asks for all li inside #items and wraps them in a jQuery object. The object is array-like: it holds matched DOM elements in order and adds methods such as .text() and .css(). It is not a DOM element.
$(document).ready(fn) runs fn after the DOM is built. The shorthand is $(fn). This is earlier than window.onload, which waits for images too.

Selectors are CSS selectors: tag, .class, #id, [attr='v']. jQuery adds its own extension selectors such as :input, which is not a CSS pseudo-class, and filters such as :first, :last, :even (0,2,4...), :odd. So $('#items li:first') is the first item.
Most methods return the same jQuery object. That is why calls chain. The set stays the same unless a method like .first() or .eq(1) narrows it.

sections.h3: Changing text, classes, elements and visibility

blocks.text: Getters and setters share one name. With no argument, .text() returns the text of the first element only. With an argument, .text('New') sets the text of every element in the set. The same pattern holds for .html() (markup), .val() (form field value), .attr('href') and .css('color','red').
Class methods: .addClass('sel'), .removeClass('sel'), .toggleClass('sel'). .data('id') reads a data-id attribute; .data('id', 7) stores a value in jQuery's data store.

Add and remove elements: .append(x) puts x inside at the end; .prepend(x) inside at the start; .before(x) and .after(x) outside; .remove() deletes the set and its events; .empty() deletes children only.

Effects: .hide(400), .show(400), .fadeIn(400), .fadeOut(400), .slideUp(400). The number is duration in milliseconds; 400 ms is 0.4 s. With no number, jQuery uses its default speed. To run code when an effect ends, pass a callback: .fadeIn(400, function(){ ... }), or use .promise().done(fn). Chaining another effect, like .fadeOut(400) after .fadeIn(400), does wait, because effects queue on the element. Ordinary methods do not wait: in .fadeIn(400).addClass('done') the class is added at once.

Event shortcuts: .click(fn) binds a click. The general form is .on('click', fn); .off('click', fn) removes it. Inside fn, this is the real DOM element, so $(this) wraps it. .each(function(i, el){...}) loops over the set; i is the index and el is the DOM element.

AJAX: $.ajax({url:'/api/items', method:'GET', dataType:'json'}).done(fn).fail(fn). dataType 'json' parses the reply into a JavaScript object. $.get(url, fn) is a short GET; $.post(url, data, fn) is a short POST. .done runs on success and .fail on error.
$.ajax returns a jqXHR object. .done() and .fail() return that same jqXHR, which is a promise, not a jQuery element set.
Chaining on an element set returns the same jQuery object. To leave jQuery and get the real DOM element, use .get(0) or [0]. $('#items')[0] is the ul itself.

figure.caption: Each call returns the same set of elements, so the dots fit on one line. The selection is made once; the later calls change and show it.

spec.title: One selection, three chained calls
spec.aria: One selection of list items flows through a colour change, a class add and a fade in; each call returns the same set.

examples.question: A page has a list with three items: Pen, Book, Bag. Write one jQuery chain that adds the class 'sel' to all three items and sets the first item's text to 'Pen (new)'. Then use .each() to print every item's text. Give the console output.
steps: Select the set: $('#items li') returns a jQuery object with 3 elements.
Add the class: .addClass('sel') adds sel to all 3 and returns the same 3-element set.
Narrow and set: .first() keeps only the first element. .text('Pen (new)') sets that element's text and returns the first element.
Loop: $('#items li').each(function(){ console.log($(this).text()); }). Inside the function, this is one DOM li; $(this) wraps it; .text() reads that one element's text.
The loop prints three lines in document order: Pen (new), Book, Bag.
examples.answer: The chain adds class sel to all three items, changes the first text to Pen (new), and the console prints Pen (new), Book, Bag on three lines.

traps: Calling .text() on a set returns only the first element's text, not all texts joined. Use .each() or .map().get().join() to collect every text.
A jQuery object is not a DOM element. $('#items') is a wrapper; $('#items')[0] or $('#items').get(0) is the real ul. Inside an event handler, this is already the DOM element.
:even and :first are zero-based jQuery filters, not CSS. :first picks one element from the whole set; CSS :first-child checks each parent separately.
.html('x') inserts markup; .text('x') inserts literal text. Putting user input through .html() can run a script, an XSS risk.
$(document).ready waits for the DOM only. window.onload waits for images and other assets too. Scripts that touch the DOM should wait for ready or sit at the end of the body.

quiz.q: What does the jQuery function $ return when you pass it a CSS selector string?
quiz.a: A jQuery object: an array-like wrapper holding the matched DOM elements, with jQuery methods added.

quiz.q: Why does $('#items li').addClass('sel').fadeIn(400) work as one chain?
quiz.a: .addClass() returns the same jQuery object, so .fadeIn() is called on the same set of elements.

quiz.q: The list has Pen, Book, Bag. What does console.log($('#items li').text()) print?
quiz.a: It prints only Pen. On a multi-element set, the .text() getter returns the first element's text.

quiz.q: Write a jQuery AJAX GET to /api/items expecting JSON, and log the reply on success.

quiz.a: .eq(0) returns a jQuery object holding the first element; .get(0) returns the raw DOM element itself.
It is shorthand for $(document).ready(function(){ ... }): run the function after the DOM is built.

quiz.q: Name two jQuery filters used after a selector.
A page runs $('#items li').remove() and later $('#items').append('New'). Is there a new list item inside #items?
quiz.a: No. .remove() deletes the old li elements and their events but keeps #items. $('#items').append('New') puts the string as a text node directly inside the ul, not as an li, so the ul just holds the text New. To add a real item use $('#items').append('<li>New</li>').

beyond: Not for the exam. In industry, jQuery still appears in old admin panels, WordPress plugins and quick prototypes, but new projects usually use fetch or a framework's data layer. The chain habit — select, change, repeat — appears again in React state updates and in Angular binding. Search next for jQuery migration guides, fetch and the $, jQuery alias in browser consoles.
